summary: Deployed a WireGuard gateway topology: node2 serves an HTTP app on TCP 8080 bound only to its private interface (10.50.50.11), reachable exclusively via a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (VyOS, wg0 10.200.0.1/24, listening on eth0's public-shared address). node3 connects as a WG client (10.200.0.2) and reaches the app at 10.50.50.11:8080 only through the tunnel; direct access from node3 to node2 over the shared 10.100.3.0/24 network is blocked (app not listening there). NAT masquerade on node1's eth1 lets node2 route return traffic back through node1 without extra routes on node2. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery (config persistence, service auto-start, tunnel re-handshake, app reachability, and continued blocking of the direct path).
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes' OS, interfaces, and routes to discover topology: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (Alpine) share a private eth1 link with no IP configured; node1/node2/node3 share a public eth0 network (10.100.3.0/24) that node3 is also on.
Assigned static private IPs: node1 eth1 10.50.50.254/24, node2 eth1 10.50.50.11/24 (persisted in /etc/network/interfaces).
Installed python3 on node2 and created an openrc 'webapp' service serving HTTP on 10.50.50.11:8080 only (not 0.0.0.0), enabled at boot.

Generated a WireGuard keypair on node1 and one on node3; configured node1 wg0 (10.200.0.1/24, port 51820, peer node3) via VyOS configure/commit/save, plus NAT source masquerade rule (wg subnet -> eth1) and permissive input/forward firewall default-actions.

Installed wireguard-tools on node3 and configured /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf as a client (10.200.0.2/24) with endpoint node1:51820 and AllowedIPs covering the WG and private LAN subnets; enabled wg-quick.wg0 at boot via OpenRC.
Verified end-to-end: node3 reaches node2's app via the tunnel (10.50.50.11:8080) and is blocked from reaching it directly over the shared network (10.100.3.11:8080).

Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, service/tunnel/app state) on all three nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time using native reboot, polling until each came back, and re-verified boot_id change plus full functional recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: App served from node2 on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: webapp openrc service started on node2 listening on 10.50.50.11:8080; curl from node1 over the private link returns the app's HTML.

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches the app only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
evidence.summary: Before binding restriction, node3 could reach node2:8080 directly (HTTP 200) which violated the requirement; after rebinding the app to 10.50.50.11 only, direct access returns HTTP 000 (connection refused) while access via the tunnel IP 10.50.50.11:8080 through wg0 succeeds.
Keys exchanged, wg0 configured on node1 (VyOS) and node3 (Alpine); wg show confirms handshake and traffic; ping and curl succeed across the tunnel.
nft ruleset shows masquerade rule for wg subnet -> eth1 and forward/input filters set to accept, enabling routed return traffic without LAN-side changes on node2.

Baseline boot_id 4098161f...; reboot acknowledged and node became unreachable then returned with boot_id c9b266ae... (changed); post-restart wg0/eth1/NAT config intact from saved VyOS config, and node3 successfully re-handshakes and reaches the app through the tunnel.

Baseline boot_id 60eadd89...; reboot triggered, node unreachable then returned with boot_id 98ae1e16... (changed); eth1 static IP and webapp service auto-recovered, and node3 confirmed app reachable via tunnel and blocked directly post-restart.

Baseline boot_id 1be8252a...; reboot triggered, node unreachable then returned with boot_id 1665a5bf... (changed); wg-quick.wg0 service auto-started, tunnel re-established (fresh handshake), app reachable via tunnel, and direct access remained blocked.
